partners.mechanism_chain: CLCN4 (HGNC:2095) —DISRUPTS→ Neuronal excitability regulation (GO:0007269); Neuronal excitability regulation (GO:0007269) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual disability (HP:0001249); CASQ2 (HGNC:2100) —DISRUPTS→ Calcium homeostasis in sarcoplasmic reticulum (GO:0005893); Calcium homeostasis in sarcoplasmic reticulum (GO:0005893) —DISRUPTS→ Intracellular calcium levels (CHEBI:15207); Intracellular calcium levels (CHEBI:15207) —LEADS_TO→ Catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (HP:0011681); Neuronal excitability regulation (GO:0007269) —LEADS_TO→ Intracellular calcium levels (CHEBI:15207). Loss-of-function mutations in CLCN4 disrupt neuronal excitability regulation, leading to intellectual disability. partners.mechanism_chain: CLCN4 (HGNC:2270) —LEADS_TO→ Intellectual Disability (HP:0001249); SCNN1A (HGNC:10596) —DISRUPTS→ Glomerular Filtration (GO:0015070); Glomerular Filtration (GO:0015070) —LEADS_TO→ Pseudohypoaldosteronism (HP:0000048); CLCN4 (HGNC:2270) —DISRUPTS→ Glomerular Filtration (GO:0015070). Loss-of-function mutations in CLCN4 lead to intellectual disability and also disrupt the function of glomerular filtration, potentially through shared downstream effects or regulatory pathways. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in SCNN1A directly disrupt glomerular filtration, leading to pseudohypoaldosteronism. The convergence on glomerular filtration as a disrupted process links these two distinct disease modules.
